description: Doenjang Jjigae is a beloved Korean classic, a hearty and comforting soybean paste stew cherished for its deep, savory flavors. This versatile dish is packed with fresh vegetables, tofu, and sometimes meat or seafood, all simmered in a rich, umami-filled broth. It is the perfect warming meal, often served bubbling hot with a bowl of rice and various banchan.

ingredients.notes: for broth, remove heads and guts

instructions.title: Prepare the Anchovy-Kelp Broth
instructions.text: In a medium pot, combine 4 cups of water, dried anchovies (heads and guts removed for cleaner taste), and dried kelp. Bring the mixture to a boil over medium-high heat. Once boiling, reduce the heat to medium-low and let it simmer gently for 15-20 minutes. Carefully remove and discard the anchovies and kelp, reserving the flavorful broth.

instructions.title: Prepare Vegetables and Other Ingredients
instructions.text: While the broth is simmering, prepare your vegetables. Peel and dice the potato into bite-sized pieces. Slice the zucchini into half-moon shapes. Slice the onion and mushrooms. Mince the garlic. Dice the firm tofu. Slice the green chili and chop the green onion. If using pork belly or beef, slice it thinly into small pieces.

instructions.title: Saute Meat and Aromatics (Optional Step)
instructions.text: If you are including meat, heat a small amount of cooking oil in a dolsot (Korean earthenware pot) or a medium pot over medium heat. Add the thinly sliced pork belly or beef and cook until it is lightly browned. Then, add the minced garlic and sliced onion to the pot, sauteing until they become fragrant and softened, about 2-3 minutes.

instructions.title: Combine Ingredients and Start Simmering
instructions.text: To the pot (with or without meat), add the diced potato, zucchini, and mushrooms. Pour in the prepared anchovy-kelp broth. Stir in the doenjang and gochujang (if using), making sure both pastes dissolve completely into the broth. Bring the stew to a boil over medium-high heat.

instructions.title: Simmer Until Vegetables Are Tender
instructions.text: Once the stew is boiling, reduce the heat to medium-low. Let the stew simmer gently for 10-15 minutes, or until the potatoes are tender when pierced with a fork. This allows the flavors to deepen and the vegetables to cook through properly.

instructions.title: Add Tofu, Chilies and Finish
instructions.text: Gently add the diced tofu and sliced green chili to the simmering stew. Continue to simmer for another 5 minutes to allow the tofu to heat through and absorb the delicious flavors. Just before serving, stir in the chopped green onions. Taste the stew and adjust seasoning if necessary, adding a little more doenjang or a pinch of salt if desired.

instructions.title: Serve Hot
instructions.text: Serve your Doenjang Jjigae immediately, piping hot, preferably in the dolsot it was cooked in if available. It is traditionally served with a bowl of freshly cooked rice and various Korean side dishes (banchan).

tips: For a deeper, richer flavor, use a good quality, aged doenjang. The taste can vary significantly between brands, so experiment to find your favorite.
Doenjang Jjigae is incredibly versatile. Feel free to add other ingredients like clams, shrimp, sliced pork shoulder, or even different vegetables like Korean radish (mu) or mushrooms.
Serve the stew bubbling hot directly from the pot (especially a dolsot) to the table. This enhances the dining experience and keeps the dish warm throughout the meal.
